mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected future dividends and equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for ≥2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 60-day prior window (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for three consecutive months, investors anticipate a premature rate cut by the Fed, which increases risk appetite and drives up equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for ≥3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day prior window (t-test p > 0.05) during the inflation spike.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly PAYEMS (labor market additions) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (unemployment) signals a tight labor market, prompting firms to raise wages and invest, which boosts equity risk premia and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥10% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by ≥0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified labor market signal window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in GDPC1 (real private consumption) of at least 2% for two consecutive months indicates weakening demand, which compresses corporate earnings growth forecasts and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by ≥2% month-over-month for ≥2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 10-day prior window (t-test p > 0.05) during the demand decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 100 for three consecutive months, after a prior expansionary phase, suggests supply-side weakness that reduces market capacity and elevates growth expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 100 and remains below for ≥3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically worse than the 30-day prior window (t-test p > 0.05) during the contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (reserves as a share of GDP) rises above 120% for two consecutive months, it indicates excess liquidity in the banking system, which lowers real interest rates and supports equity valuation expansion, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS crosses above 120% and remains above for ≥2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 10-day prior window (t-test p > 0.05) during the liquidity surge.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in HOUST (housing starts) by at least 15% in a single month, coincident with a rise in UNRATE above 4.5%, signals a cooling housing market and tighter credit conditions, which depress equity risk premia and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by ≥15% in a single month while UNRATE increases by ≥0.3 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified housing-labor signal.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months and INDPRO remains flat or slightly expanding, it suggests a labor market recovery that offsets supply-side constraints, raising growth expectations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for ≥2 consecutive months and INDPRO ≥ 100 for the same months
regime_hint: Labor market recovery in a steady supply environment
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day prior window (t-test p > 0.05) during the recovery window.
